then.text: Oh, before you go. Come here a minute. No, into the kitchen. Mind the cat's bowl.
You'll be in and out of them hedges, I know you. You'll come home with bramble in your hair and purple sleeves.
Well, if you're going to pick things, you might as well know what to do with them. Here. Your gran's recipe book.
Bakewell tart, nettle tea, a couple of snares. And some rowan business at the back she swore by. Don't laugh.
The bench is by the window. Use it whenever you're home. Wash your hands first. I mean it.
Folk all over will have their own recipes. Ask nicely, and say thank you. I'll know if you don't.
The kettle's on. It's always on. It has been on, I believe, since the Romans.
Did you know, Kit's mum rang me? She says Kit's been telling the whole street. I said 'yes, I know. Mine was in the credits.' She said 'what credits?'
Orkney, the Isle of Man, wherever it is next. Wrap up. Take a flask. Ring when you get there. Or send a raven. I'm told they're quicker.
Oh, and the Keepers have been on. All ten, one after another. They say they'd like a rematch, if you're passing. I said you'd be delighted. You'd better be.
Professor Garside says she'll rematch you too, and check your Fieldbook. And Kit's practising in the bathroom mirror. I can hear it through the wall.
Tea's in your bag. The Field Station is at the east end of town.
Look at you. My grown-up {man}, off to see the Isles. The mirror's by your bed if your hair wants a word.
And if a creature follows you home, it's NOT sleeping on the sofa.

else.text: Morning, love. Well, gone ten. You slept through the pigeons AND the bin lorry.
Professor Garside rang. Twice. Something about the stones humming.
I said you were busy being asleep. She said that was 'not an excuse'.
Off you go to the Field Station, east end of town, past the market.
And there's a noticeboard by the market stalls. Folk pin odd jobs on it. Do a few and people start to know your face.
Your garden's out the front, by the way. Plant anything you pick and it grows while you're out. That's how it got all them dandelions.
Here, take some tea. A flask is no good if it's not got tea in it.
Wrap up. And be nice to any creatures. They're only after a biscuit, same as me.

then.text: Something's ready out in that garden of yours. I could see it from the kitchen window. I've not touched it. Much.
There's a legend asleep on my lawn, love. An actual legend out of the old stories. I've put a saucer of milk out. I didn't know what else to do.
Mrs Hulme at number twelve has been twitching her nets all morning. Let her twitch.
Your diploma's up over the trophy shelf. Excellent light, as promised. I've shown the postman. Twice. He's started taking the long way round.
I've dusted your Wardstones. One of them hummed at me. I've told it we'll have none of that in this house.
All ten Wardstones on one shelf. I had to move the good china to the back bedroom. Worth it. Don't tell your nan.

cold_open.text: The moors above Macclesfield. Twenty to midnight, and not a soul about.
Then a standing stone that has kept quiet for four thousand years begins, very softly, to hum.
On the skyline, something with antlers lifts its head and listens.
Down in town, nobody noticed. Least of all you.

mirror.text: The mirror by your bed. A bit of toothpaste on it, but it does the job.
